items.text: The renewal limit check 'loan.renewals > MAX_RENEWALS' lets a third renewal through. On a loan already renewed twice (renewals == 2), renew() succeeds once more, while the README promises at most two. It should be '>='
items.evidence: seeded: shelf/loans.py renew(), README 'at most twice'

items.text: The 5.00 EUR fine cap applies only to returned books ('if loan.returned'). For a book that is still out and 40 days late, fine() and the fine command show 10.00 EUR instead of 5.00
items.evidence: seeded: shelf/loans.py fine(), README 'never goes above 5.00 EUR'

items.text: A renewal counts the new due date from today ('today + RENEW_DAYS'), not from the current due date. Renewing 5 days before the due date gives the reader 9 days instead of 14, although the README promises that renewing early never costs days. The test does not catch this because it renews exactly on the due date
items.evidence: seeded: shelf/loans.py renew(), README 'adds 14 days to the current due date', tests/test_loans.py test_renew_adds_two_weeks

items.text: save() in cli.py does not write renewals to the loan file, so every renewal through the renew command starts from zero and the renewal limit never triggers from the command line
items.evidence: seeded: shelf/cli.py save() builds raw without 'renewals', load() reads it with default 0

items.text: The renew command prints 'Renewed until None', because renew() returns nothing and cli.py prints its result instead of loan.due
items.evidence: seeded: shelf/cli.py main(), shelf/loans.py renew() has no return

errors.text: The claim that when a book is returned before the due date days_late() becomes negative and fine() gives a negative fine (in fact days_late() clamps the value with max(0, ...), and the change does not touch this code)
errors.evidence: shelf/loans.py days_late() returns max(0, ...), unchanged by the diff
